content: However, there is a lack of high-quality randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to determine the optimal level of potassium intake for maximizing health benefits. Further research is needed to clarify the precise target intake. Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Interventions aimed at reducing the burden of NCDs are valuable across all regions and income levels, as these diseases affect countries globally. While evidence from meta-analyses of cohort studies is inconclusive, there are indications that increased potassium intake may benefit cardiovascular health and reduce the risk of stroke. Cohort data specifically support the positive effect of higher potassium intake on stroke prevention. Similarly, high-quality evidence indicates no adverse effects on blood lipids, catecholamine levels, or renal function in adults with increased potassium intake. Achieving recommended potassium intake levels is feasible through the consumption of potassium-rich foods such as fresh fruits, vegetables, beans, and dairy products. However, successful implementation requires public health education, consumer awareness campaigns, and integration into existing nutrition programs at global, regional, and national levels. Reducing the burden of NCDs is highly cost-effective, and these recommendations can be incorporated into public health initiatives to promote better nutrition and health outcomes. The World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines on potassium intake for adults and children emphasize the importance of evidence-based recommendations to improve cardiovascular health and reduce the risk of chronic diseases.
